WIP: construct infinitely many roots in every nontrivial degree

Append the explicit residual-coordinate injection in the original quotient, its owning exposition, and a full-telescope audit attempt. Kernel and audit verification are pending the canonical disk gate.

WIP: prove every nontrivial root fiber is infinite

The exact original quotient now contains an explicit Nat injection into every degree-m root fiber for m>1. The D5 module compiled successfully; the full-telescope audit, source-bound reports and owning Scribe emission remain in progress.

Prove infinite root fibers in every nontrivial degree

Construct an explicit Nat injection in the original quotient for every m>1, with a nonzero residual coordinate distinguishing each root. Preserve all original declarations and proofs. Add a full-telescope source-bound audit and the owning Scribe, including the precise finite-root compactness boundary.

Validation: targeted Lean build and both scoped reports succeeded with standard-three axiom closure; the new audit is declared_validated with a source-equivalence certificate; canonical scoped Scribe emission succeeded. Integration, freeze, publication and CI remain with the caller.

Prove every nontrivial root fiber is infinite in the independent-root group

For each m>1, construct an injection from Nat into the m-root fiber of c in the existing quotient group G. Distinct roots are separated by their residual cyclic coordinates. The original G, c, root relations and no-rational-homomorphism proof are preserved.

The owning Scribe explains why the finite-root-fiber hypothesis fails at every nontrivial degree, while distinguishing this from the separate obstruction to coherent roots. No independence, topology or literature novelty claim is made.

question_answered: Are all m-root fibers of c infinite for every natural m>1, including even and composite degrees?
dominating_theorem_search: Existing quotient/projection APIs provide the coordinates; no all-degree explicit injection was found in the searched project scope.

The new full-telescope Reg audit has a source-equivalence certificate and declared_validated in its explicitly targeted module. Current integration preserves all source and report input hashes; canonical existing-member freeze updates the declaration inventory.

Wire infinite root fiber registration into canonical owner discovery

Add the existing sibling Reg import. The scoped owner report compiles only the changed owner and validates both source-equivalence registrations.

Prove quantitative spectral defect for nonerasing rich-word images

Use actual complete-return image periods and the opposite Type I/II beta coefficients to give an effective rational defect bound and its near-attainment consequence.

@@ -4,7 +4,283 @@
 
 Hanna's bilateral product family has every positive coefficient equal to two modulo four.
 
-**Theorem 1.1 (Laurent embedding preserves an inverse).**
+**Definition 1.1 (The positive-index integral term).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall k: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{positiveTerm}\left(c, A, k\right) = ((X)^{k}) \cdot ((((A)^{k}) \cdot (((A)^{k} + X)^{(c) \cdot (k) - (1)})) \cdot (((X)^{k} + A)^{(c) \cdot (k) - (1)}))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.positiveTerm` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The term at a positive index k contains X to the power k and the two polynomial factors in the bilateral product.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The negative-index integral term).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall k: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{negativeTerm}\left(c, A, k\right) = ((X)^{(c) \cdot ((k)^{2})}) \cdot ((((A)^{(c) \cdot ((k)^{2})}) \cdot ((\operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(1 + (X) \cdot ((A)^{k}), 1\right))^{(c) \cdot (k) + 1})) \cdot ((\operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(1 + ((X)^{k}) \cdot (A), 1\right))^{(c) \cdot (k) + 1}))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.negativeTerm` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Factoring the negative Laurent powers produces X to the power c*k squared and integral unit inverses.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Agreement below a degree).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\forall n: \mathbb{N}, (n < d) \implies (\operatorname{coeff}\left(n, A\right) = \operatorname{coeff}\left(n, B\right)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.Agree` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Two integer power series agree below d exactly when their coefficients at every n less than d coincide.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Agreement is divisibility by a power of X).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\operatorname{Dvd}\left((X)^{d}, A - (B)\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Agreement below d is equivalent to divisibility of the difference by X to the power d.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (A series agrees with itself).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, A\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_refl` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Every integer power series agrees with itself below every natural degree.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (Sums preserve agreement).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall G: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \implies ((\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, F, G\right)) \implies (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A + F, B + G\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_add` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Adding two pairs of series that agree below d preserves agreement below d.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (Products preserve agreement).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall G: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \implies ((\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, F, G\right)) \implies (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, (A) \cdot (F), (B) \cdot (G)\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_mul` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Multiplying two pairs of series that agree below d preserves agreement below d.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (Natural powers preserve agreement).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall k: \mathbb{N}, (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \implies (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, (A)^{k}, (B)^{k}\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_pow` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Equal coefficients below d remain equal after taking the same natural power.
+
+**Theorem 1.9 (Normalized unit inverses preserve agreement).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(A\right) = 1) \implies ((\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(B\right) = 1) \implies ((\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \implies (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, \operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(A, 1\right), \operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(B, 1\right)\right))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_inverse` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For two series of constant coefficient one, agreement below d passes to their integral unit inverses.
+
+**Theorem 1.10 (A positive shift improves agreement).**
+
+$$\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \forall k: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (0 < k) \implies ((\operatorname{Agree}\left(d, A, B\right)) \implies (\operatorname{Agree}\left(d + 1, ((X)^{k}) \cdot (A), ((X)^{k}) \cdot (B)\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.agree_shift` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Multiplication by X to any positive power improves agreement from d to d+1.
+
+**Definition 1.11 (The integral geometric series).**
+
+$$\operatorname{geometric} = \operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(1 + X, 1\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.geometric` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+This is invOfUnit(1+X,1), the normalized integral inverse of 1+X.
+
+**Theorem 1.12 (The geometric inverse identity).**
+
+$$(\operatorname{geometric}) \cdot (1 + X) = 1$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.geometric_spec` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Multiplying the geometric series by 1+X gives one.
+
+**Theorem 1.13 (The alternating geometric coefficients).**
+
+$$\forall n: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{coeff}\left(n, \operatorname{geometric}\right) = (-(1))^{n}$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.geometric_coeff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The coefficient at every natural n is (-1) to the power n.
+
+**Definition 1.14 (The integral fixed-point operator).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \operatorname{step}\left(c, A\right) = (2) \cdot (\operatorname{geometric}) - (1) + (2) \cdot ((1 + A) \cdot (\operatorname{nonzeroSum}\left(c, A\right)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.step` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural c and integer series A, the step is 2*geometric-1+2*(1+A)*nonzeroSum(c,A).
+
+**Definition 1.15 (The successive integral approximations).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, (\operatorname{approximation}\left(c, 0\right) = 1) \land (\forall d: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{approximation}\left(c, d + 1\right) = \operatorname{step}\left(c, \operatorname{approximation}\left(c, d\right)\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.approximation` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The initial approximation is one; each successor is obtained by applying step at the same parameter c.
+
+**Theorem 1.16 (The polynomial equation is the fixed-point equation).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (((1 + X) \cdot (1 + A)) \cdot (1 - ((2) \cdot (\operatorname{nonzeroSum}\left(c, A\right)))) = 2) \Leftrightarrow (A = \operatorname{step}\left(c, A\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.equation_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural c and integer series A, multiplying out the polynomial equation is equivalent to A=step(c,A).
+
+**Definition 1.17 (Embedding integer series into rational Laurent series).**
+
+$$\forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \operatorname{embed}\left(A\right) = \operatorname{HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, \operatorname{PowerSeries.map}\left(\operatorname{Int.castRingHom}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right), A\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.embed` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Map each integer coefficient to the rationals and then apply HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries with integer exponents.
+
+**Theorem 1.18 (The embedding preserves nonnegative coefficients).**
+
+$$\forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \forall n: \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{HahnSeries.coeff}\left(\operatorname{embed}\left(A\right), \operatorname{Int.ofNat}\left(n\right)\right) = \operatorname{Int.cast}\left(\operatorname{coeff}\left(n, A\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.embed_coeff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At each natural degree N, the Laurent coefficient is the rational image of the original integer coefficient.
+
+**Theorem 1.19 (The Laurent embedding is injective).**
+
+$$\operatorname{Function.Injective}\left(\operatorname{embed}\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.embed_injective` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Equality of the embedded Laurent series implies equality of the original integer power series.
+
+**Theorem 1.20 (The embedding preserves a normalized inverse).**
+
+$$\forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(A\right) = 1) \implies (\operatorname{embed}\left(\operatorname{invOfUnit}\left(A, 1\right)\right) = (\operatorname{embed}\left(A\right))^{-(1)})$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.embed_inverse` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an integer series with constant coefficient one, the embedding sends invOfUnit(A,1) to the inverse of embed(A).
+
+**Theorem 1.21 (Factoring a negative Laurent summand).**
+
+$$\forall F: \operatorname{Type}, \forall field: \operatorname{Field}\left(F\right), \forall x: F, \forall u: F, \forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall k: \mathbb{N}, (x \ne 0) \implies ((u \ne 0) \implies (((((x)^{-(k)}) \cdot ((u)^{-(k)})) \cdot (((u)^{-(k)} + x)^{-((c) \cdot (k) + 1)})) \cdot (((x)^{-(k)} + u)^{-((c) \cdot (k) + 1)}) = ((x)^{(c) \cdot ((k)^{2})}) \cdot ((((u)^{(c) \cdot ((k)^{2})}) \cdot (((1 + (x) \cdot ((u)^{k}))^{-(1)})^{(c) \cdot (k) + 1})) \cdot (((1 + ((x)^{k}) \cdot (u))^{-(1)})^{(c) \cdot (k) + 1}))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.negative_factorization` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Over any field, nonzero x and u satisfy the negative-index factorization for every natural c and k, including k=0.
+
+**Theorem 1.22 (The zero-index Laurent term).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), \operatorname{laurentTerm}\left(c, A, 0\right) = ((1 + \operatorname{embed}\left(X\right))^{-(1)}) \cdot ((1 + \operatorname{embed}\left(A\right))^{-(1)})$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.laurent_zero` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At index zero the literal summand is the product of the inverses of 1+embed(X) and 1+embed(A).
+
+**Theorem 1.23 (The zero Laurent term comes from a rational power series).**
+
+$$\forall c: \mathbb{N}, \forall A: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(A\right) = 1) \implies (\operatorname{laurentTerm}\left(c, A, 0\right) = \operatorname{HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, ((1 + X)^{-(1)}) \cdot ((1 + \operatorname{PowerSeries.map}\left(\operatorname{Int.castRingHom}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right), A\right))^{-(1)})\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Bilateral/BilateralProductModFour.zeroTerm_series` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For constant coefficient A(0)=1, the zero term is the Laurent embedding of (1+X) inverse times (1+map(A)) inverse over the rationals.
+
+**Theorem 1.24 (Laurent embedding preserves an inverse).**
 
 $$\forall B: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right), (\operatorname{constantCoeff}\left(B\right) \ne 0) \implies (\operatorname{HahnSeries}.\operatorname{ofPowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, (B)^{-(1)}\right) = (\operatorname{HahnSeries}.\operatorname{ofPowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, B\right))^{-(1)})$$

+**Lemma 3.1 (Defect identity).** For every $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ and $c\in\mathbb C$ one has $S(X+cI)=S(X)$. If $\mathrm{tr}X=0$, then
+
+$$
+S(X)=dq(1-dq)\,D^\ast D+\lambda dq\,(D^\ast Y+Y^\ast D)+\lambda(1-\lambda)\,Y^\ast Y+\mu\,\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)+q\|X\|^2 I .
+$$
+
+Stance: repo-derived.
+
+**Proof.** Since $\Phi$ is Hermiticity-preserving, $\Phi(X^\ast)=\Phi(X)^\ast$, and $\Phi(I)=I$. Expanding, $\Phi\big((X+cI)^\ast(X+cI)\big)=\Phi(X^\ast X)+\bar c\,\Phi(X)+c\,\Phi(X)^\ast+|c|^2I$ and $\Phi(X+cI)^\ast\Phi(X+cI)=\Phi(X)^\ast\Phi(X)+\bar c\,\Phi(X)+c\,\Phi(X)^\ast+|c|^2I$; the difference is $S(X)$. Now let $\mathrm{tr}X=0$ and put $a=1-dq=\lambda+\mu$. Then $\Phi(X)=aD+\lambda Y$, so $\Phi(X)^\ast\Phi(X)=a^2D^\ast D+a\lambda(D^\ast Y+Y^\ast D)+\lambda^2Y^\ast Y$. The matrices $D^\ast Y$ and $Y^\ast D$ have zero diagonal, hence $\mathrm{diag}(X^\ast X)=D^\ast D+\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)$ and
+
+$$
+\Phi(X^\ast X)=aD^\ast D+\lambda(D^\ast Y+Y^\ast D)+\lambda Y^\ast Y+\mu\,\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)+q\|X\|^2I .
+$$
+
+Subtracting and using $a-a^2=dq(1-dq)$ and $\lambda-a\lambda=\lambda dq$ gives the stated identity. ∎
+

+**定理 11.1（指定缺陷站点的精确节点因子）。** 对任意整数 $r,m\ge3$，令 $L=rm$、$q=(m-1)r+1$，在 $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$ 上取定义 6.1 的势
+
+$$
+U_i=\begin{cases}-1,&i\equiv0\pmod r\ \text{或}\ i=q,\\1,&\text{其余情形}。\end{cases}
+$$
+
+令 $t$ 为不定元，$K=\mathbb R(t)$，并记
+
+$$
+H=\Delta_L+t\operatorname{diag}(U),\qquad
+p=\det(\lambda I_L-H),\qquad
+Q=\det(\lambda I_{L-1}-H^{(q)}),\qquad
+g=\operatorname{monic\_gcd}_{K[\lambda]}(p,Q).
+$$
+
+这里 $H^{(q)}$ 是同时删除第 $q$ 行与第 $q$ 列所得的实际主子矩阵，其余对角元保持 $2+tU_i$。沿用约定 2.2、2.4，置
+
+$$
+a=2-\lambda+t,\qquad b=2-\lambda-t,\qquad
+\sigma_r=bS_{r-1}(a)-2S_{r-2}(a),\qquad
+N=r\left\lfloor\frac{m-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
+$$
+
+则在 $K[\lambda]$ 中有精确的首一恒等式
+
+$$
+\boxed{\quad g=(-1)^N\Psi_m(\sigma_r).\quad}
+$$
+
+因而 $\deg_\lambda g=N$，且 $g$ 无平方因子。
+
+**证明。** 令 $\widetilde U_i=-1$ 当且仅当 $i\equiv0\pmod r$，其余站点取 $1$，并令
+
+$$
+H_0=\Delta_L+t\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde U),\qquad
+p_0=\det(\lambda I_L-H_0).
+$$
+
+由 $\widetilde U_q=1$，有 $H=H_0-2tE_{qq}$。删除第 $q$ 行列后，两矩阵完全相同。行列式对第 $(q,q)$ 元的线性给出
+
+$$
+Q=\det(\lambda I_{L-1}-H_0^{(q)}),\qquad
+p=p_0+2tQ,\qquad
+\operatorname{monic\_gcd}(p,Q)=\operatorname{monic\_gcd}(p_0,Q).
+\tag{11.1}
+$$
+
+这里保留的是圈的主子矩阵，而非把删点后端点的对角元改成 $1$ 的路 Laplace 矩阵。零振幅不受在位秩一扰动影响，是此恒等式的本征向量表述；均匀圈上的对应见 S. Roy，[*A spectral viewpoint on the single defect tight-binding chain*](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.29467v1)，§2.1–2.2、式 (1)–(4)、(10)：其跃迁系数取 $\gamma=1$，背景常数对角元 $c$ 对应能量平移 $E=\lambda-c$，其缺陷强度对应 $2t$。此处 $H_0$ 的对角元具有周期 $r$，式 (11.1) 直接来自上述行列式线性。
+
+在周期背景 $\widetilde U$ 上，从状态 $Z_{q+1}=(z_{q+1},z_q)^{\mathsf T}$ 向前传递一个周期。因为 $q\equiv1\pmod r$，依次经过的站点 $q+1,\ldots,q+r$ 的系数是 $r-2$ 个 $a$、一个 $b$、一个 $a$。故该周期的传递矩阵为
+
+$$
+C=T(a)T(b)T(a)^{r-2},\qquad
+\det C=1,\qquad
+\operatorname{tr}C=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(a)^{r-1}T(b)\bigr)=\sigma_r,
+\tag{11.2}
+$$
+
+最后一个等式使用命题 6.9。从 $q+1$ 到 $q+L+1$ 恰经过 $m$ 个相同周期，所以背景的整圈单值矩阵是 $C^m$。由事实 3.2，实际周期边界与实际主子式满足
+
+$$
+(-1)^Lp_0=\operatorname{tr}(C^m)-2,\qquad
+(-1)^{L-1}Q=(C^m)_{21}.
+\tag{11.3}
+$$
+
+周期单值的标准对应见 G. Teschl，[*Jacobi Operators and Completely Integrable Nonlinear Lattices*](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-jac/jacop.pdf)，式 (1.28)–(1.30)、§7.1 式 (7.3)–(7.10)：取该书 Jacobi 系数 $a_{\mathrm T}(n)=-1$、$b_{\mathrm T}(n)=2+t\widetilde U_n$、谱参数 $z=\lambda$；交换该书状态 $(z_n,z_{n+1})^{\mathsf T}$ 的两个坐标，即得到本卷的 $(z_{n+1},z_n)^{\mathsf T}$ 与 $T(2+t\widetilde U_{n+1}-\lambda)$。该书判别式是单值迹的一半，因而单周期判别式为 $\sigma_r/2$，整圈的周期条件对应式 (11.3) 中的迹 $2$。
+
+取 $K$ 的代数闭包 $F$，令 $\lambda_*\in F$ 为 $p,Q$ 的任一公共根。下文把 $a,b,C,\sigma_r$ 均在 $\lambda=\lambda_*$ 处取值，仍用同一字母表示。由式 (11.1)、(11.3)，矩阵 $M=C^m$ 满足
+
+$$
+M_{21}=0,\qquad \operatorname{tr}M=2,\qquad \det M=1.
+$$
+
+若 $M_{11}=\alpha$、$M_{22}=\delta$，则 $\alpha+\delta=2$、$\alpha\delta=1$，从而 $(\alpha-1)^2=0$。域中没有非零幂零元，故 $\alpha=\delta=1$，于是
+
+$$
+C^me_1=e_1,\qquad e_1=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}.
+\tag{11.4}
+$$
+
+设
+
+$$
+s=S_{r-2}(a),\qquad v=S_{r-3}(a),\qquad h=bs-v.
+$$
+
+事实 3.2 的常系数情形给出 $T(a)^{r-2}$ 的第一列为 $(s,v)^{\mathsf T}$；也可由事实 4.1 与 $S_n$ 的递推直接读出。因此
+
+$$
+Ce_1=\begin{pmatrix}ah-s\\h\end{pmatrix}.
+\tag{11.5}
+$$
+
+现证明在这个公共根处 $h\ne0$。若 $h=0$，则 $Ce_1=-s e_1$，由式 (11.4) 得 $(-s)^m=1$，特别地 $s\ne0$。由于 $r\ge3$，多项式
+
+$$
+\bigl(-S_{r-2}(X)\bigr)^m-1\in\mathbb R[X]
+$$
+
+次数为 $m(r-2)>0$，且以 $a$ 为根。因此 $a$ 在 $\mathbb R$ 上代数，$s,v$ 也在 $\mathbb R$ 上代数。又 $h=0$ 与 $s\ne0$ 给出 $b=v/s$，故 $b$ 在 $\mathbb R$ 上代数。这迫使
+
+$$
+t=\frac{a-b}{2}
+$$
+
+在 $\mathbb R$ 上代数，与 $t$ 是不定元矛盾。于是式 (11.5) 的第二个坐标确实非零。
+
+以事实 4.1 计算式 (11.4)，有
+
+$$
+0=(C^m-I)e_1
+ =S_{m-1}(\sigma_r)Ce_1-
+   \bigl(S_{m-2}(\sigma_r)+1\bigr)e_1.
+\tag{11.6}
+$$
+
+取第二个坐标，因 $h\ne0$，得 $S_{m-1}(\sigma_r)=0$；再取第一个坐标，得 $S_{m-2}(\sigma_r)+1=0$。命题 4.2 (1) 给出这两个一元多项式的首一最大公因式为 $\Psi_m$。将其 Bézout 恒等式代入 $\sigma_r$，得到
+
+$$
+\Psi_m\bigl(\sigma_r(\lambda_*,t)\bigr)=0.
+\tag{11.7}
+$$
+
+这一步同时排除带边：$S_{m-1}(2)=m$、$S_{m-1}(-2)=(-1)^{m-1}m$ 均不为零，故任何公共根均不满足 $\sigma_r=\pm2$；标量单周期矩阵 $C=\pm I$ 已包含在被排除的 $h=0$ 情形中。
+
+还须控制最大公因式的重数。主子式 $Q\in\mathbb R[t][\lambda]$ 关于 $\lambda$ 首一且次数为 $L-1$。在 $t=0$ 处，它是对角元为 $2$、相邻非对角元为 $-1$ 的 $L-1$ 阶路矩阵的特征多项式。因此
+
+$$
+Q(\lambda,0)=\prod_{j=1}^{L-1}
+ \left(\lambda-2+2\cos\frac{\pi j}{L}\right).
+\tag{11.8}

+nonconstant characteristic-zero factor retains its degree too. Indeed
+write $C=AB$ with primitive integer factors, using Gauss' lemma.
+Both reductions are nonzero, and
+

+\le\deg A+\deg B=\deg C.
+\tag{14.7}
+$$

+nonconstant factor has nonconstant reduction.

+$\mathcal F_J$ would, by Gauss' lemma, reduce to a nonconstant common
+factor of $\mathsf C_M$ and $\overline{\mathcal F_J}$, contradicting
+(13.12). Therefore $\gcd(C_{121},\mathcal F_J)=1$. The reduced primitive
+$N_J$ divides $\mathcal F_J$ up to a rational scalar by (13.7), so
+$\gcd(C_{121},N_J)=1$.

+gcd in (13.12) gives $\gcd(C_{121},ES_*)=1$. The exact support identity
+(13.8) gives $\gcd(C_{121},H)=1$. This establishes (9.5) for the
+*original* $H$. It uses neither a degree-preservation premise for $N_J$
+nor a claim that its characteristic-zero primitive extraction commutes
+with reduction. The raw determinant and the full original norm inventory
+supply the transfer instead.

+finite, possibly empty complex affine intersection. One elementary proof
+uses their nonzero resultant over $\mathbb Q(p)$ after a generic rational

+**Proposition 4.3 (Convexity of the necessary region).** The set $K_d$ of pairs $(\lambda,q)\in\mathbb R^2$ satisfying (i)–(iv) of Theorem 4.1 is a compact convex set. Stance: repo-derived.

+**Proof.** The sets defined by (i), by (ii) and by (iv) are convex: (i) is an interval in $q$, and (ii) and (iv) are sublevel sets of the convex functions $\lambda^2+(d-1)q$ and $(d-1)\lambda^2-(d-2)\lambda+q$. On the interval $0\le q\le1/(d-1)$ the affine functions $g_1(q)=d+2-d^2q$ and $g_2(q)=1-(d-2)q$ satisfy $g_1\ge(d-2)/(d-1)>0$ and $g_2\ge1/(d-1)>0$. For positive affine functions $g_1=a_1+b_1q$ and $g_2=a_2+b_2q$, the function $h=\sqrt{g_1g_2}$ satisfies $h''=-(a_1b_2-a_2b_1)^2/(4h^3)\le0$, so $h$ is concave there. Within (i), condition (iii) reads $|\lambda|\le h(q)/\sqrt{d+2}$, which describes the region between the graphs of a concave function and its negative over an interval, a convex set. The intersection of these convex sets is $K_d$. It is closed, and bounded because (i) bounds $q$ and (ii) gives $|\lambda|\le1$. ∎

+**Proposition 4.2 (The slice $q=0$).** Let $q=0$. Then $\Phi$ is Schwarz if and only if $-1/(d-1)\le\lambda\le1$. On this slice the Schwarz maps of the family are exactly its completely positive maps. Stance: repo-derived; both proofs are given in full. The second uses only cited fact (c) (Choi's theorem) together with the Kraus form of Schur multipliers, which is proved inline: for $C=\sum_kc_kc_k^\ast\ge0$ one has $C\circ X=\sum_k\mathrm{diag}(c_k)\,X\,\mathrm{diag}(c_k)^\ast$, so $X\mapsto C\circ X$ is completely positive. The completely positive interval is read off cited fact (a)(ii).
+
+**Proof.** For $q=0$, Lemma 3.1 gives $S(X)=(1-\lambda)\big(\lambda\,Y^\ast Y+\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)\big)$ for traceless $X$, and by the invariance $S(X+cI)=S(X)$, which leaves $Y$ unchanged, the same formula holds for every $X$. If $\lambda>1$ or $\lambda<-1/(d-1)$, then (ii) or (iv) of Theorem 4.1 fails, so $\Phi$ is not Schwarz. If $0\le\lambda\le1$, both $\lambda Y^\ast Y$ and $\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)$ are positive semidefinite and $1-\lambda\ge0$. Let $-1/(d-1)\le\lambda<0$. For $v\in\mathbb C^d$, each row of $Yv$ is a sum of at most $d-1$ terms, so by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
+
+$$
+v^\ast Y^\ast Yv=\sum_i\Big|\sum_{j\ne i}y_{ij}v_j\Big|^2\le(d-1)\sum_i\sum_{j\ne i}|y_{ij}|^2|v_j|^2=(d-1)\,v^\ast\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)\,v .
+$$
+
+Hence $\lambda Y^\ast Y+\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)\ge\big(1+\lambda(d-1)\big)\,\mathrm{diag}(Y^\ast Y)\ge0$, and $S(X)\ge0$. +
+Second proof. A unital Schwarz map is positive, since $\Phi(X^\ast X)\ge\Phi(X)^\ast\Phi(X)\ge0$; applied to $J\ge0$ this gives $C=\Phi(J)\ge0$. + :=\min\{1,\,1-a^2+a^2\sqrt{1-ab}\},\\
+E_{\rm dec}^X(n)&\le U_{\rm dec}(n)
+ :=\min\{1,\,r+a\sqrt{1-a^2}\}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{58.1}
+$$

+更强地，可报告构造的四个旗标 $(i,j,\mathrm{Stop})$，$i,j\in\{F,L\}$，
+以及分解的两个旗标 $(i,\mathrm{Stop})$。对应源输入上的旗标律分别为

+\tau_{\rm dec}=a[F]+r[L],
+\tag{58.2}
+$$

+       \tau_{\rm con}\otimes\pi_{\langle s,t\rangle}^X\bigr)
+ &\le U_{\rm con}(n),\\
+D\bigl(\widehat\Psi(\pi_{\langle s,t\rangle}^X),

+ &\le U_{\rm dec}(n).
+\end{aligned}

+**Theorem 4.1 (Necessary conditions).** If $\Phi$ is Schwarz, then
+
+- (i) $0\le q\le 1/(d-1)$;
+- (ii) $\lambda^2\le 1-(d-1)q$;
+- (iii) $(d+2)\lambda^2\le(d+2-d^2q)\big(1-(d-2)q\big)$;
+- (iv) $(d-1)\lambda^2-(d-2)\lambda\le1-q$, equivalently $(1-\lambda)\big(1+(d-1)\lambda\big)\ge q$.
+
+Stance: (i) and (ii) follow from cited fact (b)(i) applied with $c_{kj}=q$, $c_{jj}=p$ and $\lambda_{ij}=\lambda$, and are literature-attested; (iii) and (iv) are suspected-novel (see §7). The proof below is self-contained.
+
+**Proof.** (i), (ii). For $X=E_{12}$, $X^\ast X=E_{22}$ and $\Phi(X)=\lambda E_{12}$, so $S(E_{12})=\Phi(E_{22})-\lambda^2E_{22}=(p-\lambda^2)E_{22}+q(I-E_{22})$. Hence $q\ge0$ and $\lambda^2\le p$, and then $(d-1)q\le1-\lambda^2\le1$.
+
+(iii). Put $r=1-(d-2)q$. For real $y$ let $X_y=E_{11}-E_{22}+y(E_{12}-E_{21})$ and $v=e_1+e_2$. A direct computation with Lemma 3.1 gives
+
+$$
+v^{T}S(X_y)\,v=4\left(\frac{q(d+2-d^2q)}{2}+\lambda dq\,y+\frac{r-\lambda^2}{2}\,y^2\right).
+$$
+
+If $q=0$, inequality (iii) reads $\lambda^2\le1$ and follows from (ii). If $q>0$, then (ii) gives $r-\lambda^2\ge r-p=q>0$; taking $y=-\lambda dq/(r-\lambda^2)$, nonnegativity yields $q(d+2-d^2q)(r-\lambda^2)\ge\lambda^2d^2q^2$. Dividing by $q$ and rearranging, $(d+2-d^2q)\,r\ge\lambda^2(d^2q+d+2-d^2q)=(d+2)\lambda^2$, which is (iii).
+
+(iv). Let $X=\sum_{j=2}^{d}E_{1j}$ and $u=\sum_{j=2}^{d}e_j$. Then $X^\ast X=uu^{T}$, $\Phi(X)=\lambda X$, $\mathrm{diag}(uu^{T})=I-E_{11}$ and $\mathrm{tr}(uu^{T})=d-1$, so $S(X)=\lambda(1-\lambda)uu^{T}+\mu(I-E_{11})+(d-1)qI$. Hence
+
+$$
+u^{T}S(X)\,u=(d-1)\Big((d-1)\lambda(1-\lambda)+\mu+(d-1)q\Big)=(d-1)\Big(1-q+(d-2)\lambda-(d-1)\lambda^2\Big),
+$$
+
+and nonnegativity is (iv). The equivalent form follows from $1+(d-2)\lambda-(d-1)\lambda^2=(1-\lambda)(1+(d-1)\lambda)$. ∎
+
